detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
In addition polymerisation, many alkene monomers join because the carbon–carbon double bonds open. No small molecule is eliminated.

To draw a repeating unit, change C=C to C–C, keep attached groups on the same carbon atoms, put the repeat section in brackets, show bonds extending through both sides of the brackets and write n outside.
The polymer name is formed from the monomer name, for example ethene forms poly(ethene).
Many alkene molecules can join to form a long-chain polymer. The small starting molecules are monomers. In addition polymerisation, the C=C double bonds open and link monomers into a chain.
A polymer is represented using a repeating unit inside brackets with an n outside to show many repeats.
